title: Hash tables
summary: Buckets, collisions, resizing and the equals/hashCode contract behind O(1) lookups.

questions.prompt: Hash-table lookups are O(1) on average. What makes them slower in bad cases?
options: Many keys landing in the same bucket, which then has to be searched
The table re-sorting itself on every insert
Hashing a key taking time proportional to the number of entries
Every lookup scanning the whole table

questions.prompt: True or false: if two objects are equal according to equals, they must return the same hashCode.
A class overrides equals but not hashCode. Two equal instances are added to a HashSet. What usually happens?
options: The set keeps both: their default hash codes differ, so they land in different buckets and equals is never compared
The set keeps one, because equals is always checked first
It throws an exception on the second add

questions.prompt: A HashMap grows when its size passes capacity × load factor (0.75 by default). Why is put still O(1) on average despite occasional resizing?
options: Resizing rehashes every entry, O(n), but the table doubles each time, so that cost spreads out to O(1) amortized per put
Resizing is O(1) because entries move lazily
It isn't: put is O(log n) because of resizing

questions.prompt: Group a list of words so that anagrams (like 'listen' and 'silent') end up together. Which approach?
options: A HashMap from each word's sorted letters to its group
